citation: Hoydis J. et al. (2023) Sionna RT: differentiable ray tracing for radio propagation modeling. IEEE Globecom Workshops.
description: Sionna is an open-source Python library for research on communication systems, made of three packages: Sionna RT, a fast stand-alone ray tracer for radio propagation modelling built on the Mitsuba 3 renderer; Sionna PHY, a link-level simulator for wireless and optical communication systems; and Sionna SYS, a system-level simulator based on physical-layer abstraction. Its components are differentiable and GPU accelerated, so propagation and link models can be used inside machine-learning training loops. It is developed by NVIDIA research (NVlabs) to support 5G and 6G research; the current release is 2.1, which requires Python 3.11 or later and PyTorch 2.9 or later. Coverage: any scene the user supplies, from rooms to city districts, typically imported from 3D building models such as OpenStreetMap extrusions; results are at the resolution of the scene mesh. Format and access: pip-installable Python packages and source on GitHub, with extensive documentation and tutorials; free of charge under the Apache 2.0 licence. Caveats: ray tracing needs detailed 3D scenes and material properties; a GPU is strongly recommended; large urban scenes are memory hungry. Simulation uses: coverage and hazard exposure studies of mobile networks, capacity planning of base stations, and radio digital twins of cities. Related records: NVIDIA Aerial Omniverse Digital Twin builds on it, ns-3 3.48 includes a Sionna RT channel model, and Wireless InSite is a commercial ray-tracing alternative.
